violation_type.title: Caregiver Qualification Age Exemption Attends High School - Not in Charge of Group (26 TAC §744.1107(b)(1))
violation_type.short_title: Caregiver Qualification Age Exemption Attends High School - Not in Charge of Group
violation_type.typical_finding: High School caregiver was observed supervising children while caregiver in charge was attending the cafeteria main entrance door.     Operation became in compliance when program director arrived.

finding_variants.text: High School caregiver was observed supervising children while caregiver in charge was attending the cafeteria main entrance door.     Operation became in compliance when program director arrived.

It was found during the investigation that a caregiver who was under the age of 18, attending high school and has no proof of enrollment or completion of a child-care related course was left alone with sole responsibility of caring for children.

The qualified caregiver assigned to the unqualified caregiver was not in the room at all times. Caregiver without qualifications was contantly left alone with sole responsibility of a group of children (3, 4, 5th graders).

An 18-year-old high school student was observed alone supervising children during outdoor time and in the cafeteria.     Corrected during inspection by reminding site director that High school caregiver cannot be left alone. caregiver child ratio was in compliance.     Program director arrived and was at the site until program closed for the day.
Two high school students were observed at the playground supervising children while the qualified caregiver was inside the cafeteria dealing with a parent signing a child out.
During the inspection I observed a seventeen year old caregiver take children to the restroom alone without another caregiver present.
